'''Yanjon''' was one of the [[Four Sages of Dwartii/Legends|Four Sages of Dwartii]], ancient controversial [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophers]] and lawgivers of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The other three Sages were [[Sistros/Legends|Sistros]], [[Braata/Legends|Braata]], and [[Faya/Legends|Faya]]. [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] owned a statue of Yanjon, which later passed into the hands of [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In the now defunct MMORPG ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', all four statues of the Sages of Dwartii could be collected. However, the statue that was labeled as Yanjon's in ''Galaxies''<ref name="SWG:C8">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other}}Chapter 8: The Nova Orion Crisis</ref> was identified as Braata's effigy in the bronze statues set "Sistros and Braata" produced by [[Sideshow Collectibles]].<ref name="SSC">{{WebCite|url=http://www.sideshowtoy.com/collectibles/product-archive/?sku=7232|text=Sistros and Braata: Secret Origins of the Sith|work=SideshowCollectibles.com|archiveurl=https://archive.is/6otEg}}</ref> [[Leland Chee]], administrator of the [[Holocron continuity database]] at [[Lucasfilm]], has since commented that the Sideshow identification was correct<ref name="Twit">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/382980658861076480|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=@reeldefiction Sideshow Sistros and Braata is correct. Yanjon & Faya are two other statues, though neither has yet to be specifically ID'd.|archivedate=20190722093252}}</ref> and that the statue wearing a helmet was Braata's and not Yanjon's.<ref name="Twit2">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/3840816051718799360|[[Leland Chee]]|nobackup=1}}</ref>
